claim: Gross writes that anaesthetics should be given only in the event of thorough reaction, and that while the vital powers are depressed by shock or loss of blood their administration will hardly be safe.

source.edition: S. D. Gross, A Manual of Military Surgery, second edition, Philadelphia: J. B. Lippincott & Co., 1862 (entered 1861); clean OCR; the archive.org record dates it 1861

quote: Anaesthetics should be given only in the event of thorough reaction; so long as the vital powers are depressed and the mind is bewildered by shock, or loss of blood, their administration will hardly be safe

data.name_period: anaesthetic given only after reaction from shock

claim: Tripler writes that he would give chloroform after the battle was over, in the hospital and not on the field, its administration being unnecessary and impracticable in battle.

source.edition: Tripler and Blackman, Hand-book for the Military Surgeon, third edition, Cincinnati: Robert Clarke & Co., 1862

quote: I would give chloroform after the battle was over, in the hospital not on the field. Its administration is unnecessary and impracticable in battle.

data.name_period: chloroform given in the hospital after the battle, not on the field

notes: Tripler's own view; the same book quotes Macleod and Larrey for early anaesthesia: a conflict of practice for the group to carry (topic withheld)
